title: Joint Targeting Specialist (MGySgt to SSgt) FMOS, DC PP&O POG- 70
raw_text:
17.     MOS 8036, Joint Targeting Specialist (MGySgt to SSgt) FMOS, DC PP&O POG-
70

    a. Summary. Joint Targeting Specialist serves as the targeting subject
matter expert to the commander and staff for all lethal and non-lethal fires
and effects in shaping the enemy to meet the commander's intents. These
duties include planning, integrating, coordinating, through targeting working
groups and targeting boards. This MOS will be assigned only as FMOS.
Authority to issue this additional MOS will remain with the local command
delegated to the unit level. This MOS is held by SNCOs only.

    b. Prerequisites.          Security requirement:   SCI security clearance
eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Must complete the Joint Targeting Staff Course
(N46HFS3), Dam Neck, Va.

    d. Duties. Upon completion of the Joint Targeting Staff Course and
participating in a unit/staff's targeting working group and targeting board
the individual will meet all eligibility for the certification of this MOS,
the individual recipient shall coordinate with their unit administration
department to ensure this MOS is added to their official military personnel
file (OMPF) in order to accurately reflect the corresponding targeting
qualification/designation within their permanent record.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Artillery and Missile Crew Member 55-3014.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Intelligence Specialist, 0231.

            (2) Information Specialist, 0551.

            (3) Fire Support Marine, 0861.

            (4) Fires and Effects Integrator, 0871.

            (5) Joint Terminal Attack Controller, 8002.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
